punchline: Barry Schwartz was happy with a mediocre wine because the shop only had about a dozen to choose from.
thirty_sec: On vacation on the Oregon coast, Barry Schwartz buys wine at a tiny grocery with about a dozen bottles. What he gets isn't very good, and he's perfectly satisfied, because he expected nothing better. In a store with thousands of wines, the same bottle would have disappointed him. His point: more options raise expectations, and we judge results against those expectations.
